output.subject: We've received your complaint about the power of attorney refusals
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us about your experience arranging power of attorney for your father. We have received your complaint, and we're sorry for the frustration this has caused you.

You told us that your father, who is 90, gave you power of attorney in March using the state statutory form, notarized. You mentioned that on two visits to our Elm & 4th branch, staff declined to accept it because it was "not on our form," and that on your third visit a different banker accepted it in about five minutes. You also told us that in the meantime you covered your father's bills from your own account. You've asked us to explain why the staff you spoke with did not seem to know the bank's own policy, and you pointed out that your family has banked with us for 50 years.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint, and we will respond within 10 business days.

Thank you for taking the time to tell us about this, and for your family's long relationship with Meridian Harbor Bank.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Mode is ACKNOWLEDGE ONLY: draft takes no position on whether the POA should have been accepted at the first visits.
Customer says their father is 90; consider whether vulnerable-customer handling applies.
⟦NAME_2⟧ (50-year customer) may be the father or another person; draft refers to the family generally, so confirm wording.
Customer covered father's bills from their own account; confirm whether any follow-up on this is needed (no compensation was requested).
Confirm the date and staff involved at the Elm & 4th branch visits before the substantive response.
Customer's explicit request is an explanation of staff knowledge of POA policy; ensure the final response addresses it.
